en: The Sutra Spoken by Vimalakīrti, Scroll One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by Imperial Decree.
Chapter One: The Introduction. Chapter One: The Introduction.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the Bhagavān was dwelling in the city of Vaiśālī, in the Āmrapālī Grove,
together with a great assembly of eight thousand bhikṣus and thirty-two thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all of whom were [leaders] of the entire multitude.
As I look upon those who have mastered great supernormal powers and perfected their cultivation, who are constantly sustained by the majestic virtue of all Buddhas,
who well protect the city of the Dharma and are able to uphold the True Dharma, who proclaim it with the roar of a great lion,
whose beautiful voices resound afar throughout the ten directions, and who act as uninvited spiritual friends for all sentient beings, continuing the lineage of the Three...
They can cause the lineage of jewels to remain unbroken; they subdue the enmity of Māras and restrain all non-Buddhists;
they are forever free from all hindrances, obscurations, and entanglements; their mindfulness, concentration, and dhāraṇīs are without exception perfected;
they establish the gate of unobstructed wisdom of liberation; and they attain all the dhāraṇīs of uninterrupted, supreme mindfulness, wisdom, and meditative absorption.

They were eloquent bhikṣuṇīs; they had all attained the foremost pāramitās of generosity, discipline, tranquility, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, sublime aspiration, power, and knowledge. They had perfected the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena through non-apprehension, and were able to turn the irreversible wheel of Dharma in accordance with the truth. All were sealed by the sublime seal of signlessness and possessed excellent knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties of sentient beings. They could not be overcome by any assembly and were able to guide others with fearlessness.

Having accumulated inexhaustible stores of merit and wisdom, their bodies were adorned with the primary and secondary marks of excellence, their physical form being supreme. They had renounced all worldly ornaments, and their renown was so lofty as to surpass that of Śakra. Their resolve was as firm as a diamond.

He has attained indestructible faith in all Buddha-dharmas; he causes the light of the Dharma-jewel to flow and rains down the nectar of immortality. Among all vocal expressions, his is the most subtle and supreme;

regarding the profound meaning of the Dharma and the vast dependent origination, he has severed the continuity of the habitual tendencies of the two extreme views. He expounds the Dharma with fearlessness like the roar of a lion; his preaching is like a thunderclap, immeasurable and beyond the reach of measurement.
Having gathered the wisdom of the Dharma-jewel, he is a great guide—upright, discerning, gentle, and subtle; he wondrously masters all dharmas that are difficult to see and difficult to know.

They penetrate all profound and ultimate meanings, and their aspirations take refuge in both the realms of existence and non-existence; they have obtained the consecration of the peerless Buddha-wisdom and draw near to the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique Buddha-qualities.

Having eliminated all terrors of the evil destinies, they have further transcended all treacherous, foul, and deep pits; having forever cast away the diamond sword and staff of dependent origination, they constantly contemplate manifesting births within the various realms of existence.
Acting as great kings of physicians who skillfully master medical arts, they prescribe medicine according to the ailment, curing diseases and bestowing peace.
They have fully accomplished immeasurable merits and purified immeasurable Buddha-lands; those who see or hear them all receive benefit.
Whatever they do is never in vain; even if one were to praise their merits for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas, one could not exhaust them. Their names are:
Bodhisattva Equal Contemplation, Bodhisattva Unequal Contemplation, Bodhisattva Equal and Unequal Contemplation, and Bodhisattva Stabilized Spirit.
The Bodhisattva King of Transformation, the Bodhisattva Sovereign of Dharma, the Bodhisattva Banner of Dharma, the Bodhisattva Banner of Light,
the Bodhisattva Adorned with Light, the Bodhisattva Greatly Adorned, the Bodhisattva Jewel Peak, the Bodhisattva Peak of Eloquence,
the Bodhisattva Jewel Hand, the Bodhisattva Jewel-Seal Hand, the Bodhisattva Constantly Raised Hand, and the Bodhisattva Constantly Lowered [Hand].
The Bodhisattva Hasta, the Bodhisattva Nityotkṣiptahasta, the Bodhisattva Nityapramuditendriya, the Bodhisattva Nityapramuditarāja,
the Bodhisattva Apratihata-pratibhāna, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, the Bodhisattva Ratnolkādhara,
the Bodhisattva Ratnaśrī, the Bodhisattva Ratnadatta, the Bodhisattva Indrajāla, and the Bodhisattva Jālinīprabha.
...the Bodhisattva Unobstructed Meditative Concentration, the Bodhisattva Peak of Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Heavenly King,
the Bodhisattva Destroyer of Māras, the Bodhisattva Lightning Heaven, the Bodhisattva King of Manifesting Miraculous Transformations, the Bodhisattva Adorned with Peak-like Features,
the Bodhisattva Lion’s Roar, the Bodhisattva Cloud Thunder Sound, and the Bodhisattva King of Mountain Collisions.
Gandhahastin Bodhisattva, Mahāgandhahastin Bodhisattva, Nityodyukta Bodhisattva, Anikṣiptadhura Bodhisattva,
Suviśuddhamati Bodhisattva, Sujāta Bodhisattva, Padmavijitagarbha Bodhisattva,
Samādhirāja Bodhisattva, Padmavyūha Bodhisattva, and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
...the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the Bodhisattva Brahmajāla, the Bodhisattva Ratnadaṇḍa,
the Bodhisattva Aparājita, the Bodhisattva Mārajit, the Bodhisattva Kṣetravyūha, the Bodhisattva Suvarṇacūḍa,
the Bodhisattva Maṇicūḍa, the Bodhisattva Maitreya, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, and the Bodhisattva Ratnacchattra, as...
There were thirty-two thousand such leading bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

Furthermore, there were ten thousand Brahmās, with the Brahmā King Śikhin as their leader, who had come from the Great Four-Continent World of Fundamental Sorrowless to join this assembly, desiring to behold, pay homage to, and make offerings to the World-Honored One, and to hear the Dharma.

Additionally, there were twelve thousand Śakras, each having come from other Great Four-Continent Worlds to join this assembly, likewise desiring to behold, pay homage to, and make offerings to the World-Honored One, and to hear the Dharma.
Furthermore, other gods of great power—nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, Brahmā, the World Protectors, and so forth—all came to the assembly and sat down;
as did the fourfold assembly of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, all coming together to sit in the assembly.

At that time, the World-Honored One was surrounded with reverence by an assembly of immeasurable hundreds of thousands who had gathered; he preached the Dharma for them—like the Great Jewel King of Mountains, Sumeru, towering loftily above the great ocean—seated upon the supreme lion throne of the Victorious Treasury, his radiant majesty outshining the entire multitude.

At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the city of Vaiśālī belonging to the Licchavi clan, named Ratnagotra. Accompanied by five hundred Licchavi youths, each holding a parasol adorned with the seven precious gems, he went to the Āmra grove to the place where the Tathāgata was. Having arrived, they each offered their parasols to the World-Honored One; having made the offering, they prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, circumambulated him seven times to the right, and withdrew to stand to one side.

By the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, all those jeweled canopies were merged into a single canopy that completely covered the trichiliocosm, and the vast dimensions and characteristics of this world were all manifested within it.

Furthermore, all the great jewel Sumeru Kings of this trichiliocosm—every Snowy Mountain, Mount Mucilinda, Mount Mahāmucilinda, Fragrant Mountain, Jewel Mountain, Gold Mountain, Black Mountain, Cakravāḍa Mountains, and Mahācakravāḍa Mountains; the great oceans, rivers, ponds, springs, and pools; as well as the hundred koṭis of the four great continents, the sun, moon, stars, celestial palaces, dragon palaces, and the palaces of various honored deities; together with all kingdoms, cities, royal capitals, and villages—all these appeared within this precious canopy.
Furthermore, the true Dharma taught by all Buddhas and Tathāgatas throughout the worlds of the ten directions was like an echo; within this canopy, there was nothing that was not seen or heard.

At that time, the great assembly, beholding the Buddha’s supernatural power, leaped for joy and marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence. With palms joined, they paid homage to the Buddha, gazing up at his venerable countenance without averting their eyes for even a moment, remaining in silent reverence.
At that time, Ratnagotra knelt with his right knee on the ground before the Buddha, joined his palms in reverence, and praised the Buddha with these exquisite verses:
“Your eyes are pure, long, and wide, most exquisitely beautiful, Bright as the petals of a deep blue lotus;
Having realized the foremost pure intention, You have reached the further shore of supreme śamatha.”
Having long accumulated boundless pure karma, you have attained vast and supreme renown;
therefore, I prostrate to the Great Śramaṇa, who reveals the path of the ineffable and tranquil.
Having seen the Great Sage manifest his spiritual transformations, appearing universally throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions,
wherein all Buddhas expound the Dharma— all these he now sees and hears entirely.
The Dharma King’s power of Dharma transcends all living beings; He constantly bestows the wealth of Dharma upon all.
He is able to skillfully discern the characteristics of all phenomena, And by contemplating the ultimate truth, he subdues his enemies.
Having attained mastery over all dharmas, I therefore bow my head to this Dharma King.
The teaching of the Dharma is neither existent nor non-existent; all things arise established through causes and conditions.
There is no self, no creator, and no experiencer, yet the karma of good and evil never perishes.
Originally at the Bodhi tree, he subdued the power of Māra; He attained the supreme enlightenment of the extinction of ambrosia.
Within this, there is no mental activity or sensory experience; It is that which cannot be fathomed by outsiders or the various heretics.
The Wheel of Dharma was turned three times throughout the great trichiliocosm; that wheel is capable of stilling, for its intrinsic nature is quiescent.
This rare Dharma-wisdom is realized by devas and humans, and thus the Three Jewels appeared in the world.
Using this wondrous Dharma to save all beings, Free from thought and fear, eternally peaceful and still;
The Great Physician King who delivers them from birth, old age, and death— I prostrate to the ocean of boundless merit.
Unshakable by the eight worldly concerns like the king of mountains, Compassionate toward both the virtuous and the non-virtuous,
With a mind that acts like space, abiding in equanimity— Who would not revere this Muni?
Offering this humble canopy to the World-Honored One, Within it, the palaces of the devas, nāgas, and spirits, And the entire trichiliocosm are universally manifested;
Therefore, I pay homage to the body of wisdom, vision, and merit.
The Ten-Powered One displays supernatural transformations to the world, all of which are like reflections and shadows;
seeing them, the multitude marvels at such an unprecedented occurrence, and thus they pay homage to the Great Wisdom-Vision of the Ten-Powered One.
The assembly gazes upon the Great Muni, and there is none whose mind does not give rise to pure faith;
each person perceives the World-Honored One standing before them—this is the unique characteristic of the Tathāgata.
When the Buddha expounds the Dharma with a single voice, sentient beings each attain understanding according to their own kind.
All believe that the World-Honored One speaks their own language; this is a unique characteristic of the Tathāgata.
When the Buddha expounds the Dharma with a single voice, sentient beings each understand it according to their own capacity;
they all receive and practice it to obtain its benefit; this is a unique characteristic of the Tathāgata.

When the Buddha expounds the Dharma with a single voice, some are struck with awe, some are filled with joy, some give rise to weary detachment, and some sever their doubts; this is the unique characteristic of the Tathāgata.
I bow my head to the One of Ten Powers, truthful and courageous; I bow my head to the one who has attained fearlessness;
I bow my head to the one who has reached the uncommon states of meditative concentration; I bow my head to all the Great Teachers;
I bow my head to the one who can sever all fetters and bonds; I bow my head to the one who has already dwelt upon the further shore.
I bow my head to the one who universally delivers all suffering sentient beings; I bow my head to the one who does not rely on the realms of birth and death.
Having reached the state of equality among all sentient beings, His mind is well-liberated from all realms of existence.
The Muni has thus skillfully cultivated emptiness, Just as a lotus flower is unsullied by water.
All marks are dispelled yet there is nothing dispelled; all vows are fulfilled yet there is no vow.
With inconceivable and great majestic power, I prostrate to the one who dwells nowhere, like space.
At that time, having spoken these verses in praise of the World-Honored One, the youth Ratnākara addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“These five hundred youths, all bodhisattvas, have already set out for anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi; they have all questioned me regarding the adornment and purification of buddha-fields.”
“I only pray that the Tathāgata, out of compassion, will explain the characteristics of the purification of a buddha-field.
How does a bodhisattva cultivate the purification of a buddha-field?
Having spoken these words, the Buddha said:
“Ratnagotra! Excellent, excellent!

It is well that you are now able to inquire of the Tathāgata regarding the characteristics of the purification of Buddha-fields for all bodhisattvas, and to ask about the bodhisattva’s cultivation of the purification of Buddha-fields.”
"Listen now attentively and reflect upon it well; I shall analyze and explain it for you.
Thereupon, Ratnākara and all the bodhisattvas spoke thus:
"Excellent, World-Honored One!"
"We only pray that you will explain this for us; we all now hope to hear and receive it.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bodhisattvas:
"The realms of sentient beings are the pure buddha-fields of bodhisattvas."
Why is this so? Sons of good family!
All bodhisattvas, in accordance with the growth and benefit of sentient beings, thereby embrace and purify buddha-fields.
In accordance with the various pure merits initiated by sentient beings, they immediately take hold of and purify Buddha-fields;
in accordance with the manner in which sentient beings should be tamed by such purified Buddha-fields, they immediately take hold of such Buddha-fields;
and in accordance with the way sentient beings should enter into the Buddha-wisdom through such purified Buddha-fields, they immediately take hold of such Buddha-fields.

According to the needs of sentient beings, by means of such adornments and purifications of a Buddha-field to give rise to the practice of noble faculties, he immediately takes possession of such a Buddha-field. Why is this so?
"O sons of noble family!
When Bodhisattvas embrace and purify Buddha-fields, it is entirely for the sake of increasing, benefiting, and inspiring various pure merits in sentient beings."
"O sons of good family!

It is as if there were a person who wished to construct a palace upon an empty plot of ground, or to adorn it according to their will without hindrance; yet, in the midst of space, such a thing could never be accomplished."

In this way, the bodhisattva knows that all phenomena are like space; yet, solely for the sake of increasing, benefiting, and generating pure merit for sentient beings, they then take hold of such a buddha-field.
One who takes hold of such a pure buddha-field does not do so in emptiness.
"Furthermore, Jewel-nature!
You all should know this:"

The land of generating the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment is the bodhisattva’s purified buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, all sentient beings who have generated the Mahāyāna mind come to be born in that land.

The land of pure intention is the bodhisattva’s purified buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, all sentient beings who are without guile and without deception come to be born in that land.

The land of excellent application is the bodhisattva’s purified buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, all sentient beings who have initiated and maintain sublime and virtuous applications come to be born in that land.

A land of superior intention is the bodhisattva’s pure buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, sentient beings who are fully accomplished in wholesome dharmas come to be born in that land.

A land of practicing generosity is the bodhisattva’s pure buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, all sentient beings capable of relinquishing wealth and Dharma come to be born in that land.

A land of practicing pure ethical discipline is the bodhisattva’s pure buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, sentient beings whose intentions are perfected in the ten paths of wholesome action come to be born in that land.

The land of cultivating patience is the bodhisattva’s purified buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, sentient beings who are patient, gentle, and tranquil will come to be born in that land.

The land of cultivating diligence is the bodhisattva’s purified buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, sentient beings who are virtuous, courageous, and diligent will come to be born in that land.

The land of cultivating meditative concentration is the bodhisattva’s purified buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, sentient beings who are fully endowed with right mindfulness, right awareness, and right concentration will come to be born in that land.

Cultivating the land of *prajñā* is the bodhisattva’s purification of a buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment (*mahābodhi*), all sentient beings who have entered the correct determination (*samyaktvaniyāma*) will come to be born in that land.

The land of the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) is the bodhisattva’s purification of a buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, all sentient beings who dwell constantly in loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity will come to be born in that land.

The land of the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) is the bodhisattva’s purification of a buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, all sentient beings who are embraced by liberation will come to be born in that land.

The land of skillful means is the bodhisattva’s pure buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, sentient beings who have skillfully observed all phenomena come to be born in that land.

The land cultivated through the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment is the bodhisattva’s pure buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, sentient beings who have mastered all the foundations of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of power, faculties, powers, factors of enlightenment, and path-factors in their perfection come to be born in that land.
The land cultivated through dedication is the bodhisattva’s pure buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great enlightenment, that land is fully adorned with a multitude of virtues.

Skillfully teaching the cessation of the eight states of non-leisure is the bodhisattva’s purification of a buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great awakening, that land will forever be free from the miserable realms and states of non-leisure.

Maintaining one's own ethical conduct without disparaging the conduct of others is the bodhisattva’s purification of a buddha-field; when the bodhisattva realizes great awakening, that land will not even have the name of "transgressing prohibitions. The ten paths of wholesome action as an utterly pure land is the bodhisattva’s purification of a buddha-field;

when the bodhisattva realizes great awakening, sentient beings who are born in that land will possess a fixed lifespan, great wealth, and pure conduct; their speech will be truthful, they will always speak with gentle words, their retinues will never be separated from them, they will skillfully explain the hidden intent [of the teachings], be free from all greed, have no anger in their hearts, and hold right view.
"O sons of noble family!
In this way, as soon as a bodhisattva generates the mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta), there arises a pure intention;
following that pure intention, there arises sublime and virtuous application; and following that sublime and virtuous application, there arises the superior [spiritual power]."
Regarding the intention: according to its predominant intention, there is cessation; according to its cessation, there is arousal;
according to its arousal, there is dedication; according to its dedication, there is tranquility;
according to its tranquility, there is the purification of sentient beings; and according to the purification of sentient beings, there is...
They purify the Buddha-fields; according to the purification of the Buddha-fields, there is the pure teaching of the Dharma;
according to the purity of the teaching of the Dharma, there is pure and wondrous merit;
according to pure and wondrous merit, there is pure and wondrous wisdom; according to pure and wondrous wisdom, there is pure and wondrous knowledge; according to that...
When there is pure and wondrous wisdom, there is pure and wondrous conduct; following that pure and wondrous conduct, there is a pure and wondrous mind;
and following that pure and wondrous mind, there are pure and wondrous merits.
“O sons of good family!
Therefore, if a bodhisattva wishes to diligently cultivate the purification of a Buddha-field, they should first employ skillful means to purify their own mind. Why is this?
"According to the purification of the minds of the bodhisattvas themselves, they shall obtain such purified Buddha-fields.
At that time, Śāriputra, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, had this thought:
"If it is because the minds of the bodhisattvas are purified that the Buddha-fields are purified..."
"Yet, because my mind was not purified when I practiced as a bodhisattva, this buddha-field is thus defiled and impure?
The Buddha, knowing his thought, immediately addressed him, saying:
"What do you think? What is your opinion on this?"
"Are not the sun and moon in this world pure?
Yet the blind do not see them.
He replied:
"No, this is the fault of the blind man, not the fault of the sun and moon.
The Buddha said:
"In this way, it is because of the faults of sentient beings that they do not see the sublime purity of the World-Honored One’s Buddha-land; it is not the fault of the Tathāgata.
Śāriputra, my land is pure and sublime, yet you do not see it."
At that time, the Brahma King Śikhin said to Śāriputra:
"Do not harbor the thought that this buddha-field is not adorned and pure. Why is this?
"Such is the most supremely adorned and pure Buddha-field.
Śāriputra said, "Great Brahmā King!"
"How, then, is this buddha-field adorned and purified?
The Brahmā Śikhin replied,
"Indeed, Śāriputra!"

Just as the palace of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas is adorned with the merits of immeasurable jewels, so too did I see the land of the World-Honored One, Śākyamuni Buddha, purified and adorned with the merits of immeasurable jewels.
Śāriputra said: “Great Brahmā King!
I see that this land is uneven—filled with hills and valleys, pits and hollows, poisonous thorns, gravel, sand, earth, stones, and various mountains; it is replete with impurities and foulness.”
The Brahma Śikhin said:
"O Great Honored One!
Because the mind has high and low [distinctions] and is not pure, one perceives the Buddha’s wisdom and intention to be likewise; therefore, one sees the Buddha-land as impure."

If bodhisattvas possess a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings and are adorned with pure merit—such that their aspiration for the wisdom of a Buddha is likewise—they will perceive the buddha-field as supremely pure and adorned.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing that the great assembly harbored doubts in their hearts, pressed this great earth with his toe.
Immediately, the trichiliocosm was adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of wondrous jewels, like the land of Immeasurable Merit-Jewel Adornments belonging to the Buddha Guṇaratnavyūha.
The entire assembly marveled at what they had never before experienced, and each saw themselves seated upon a precious lotus flower.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śāriputra:
“Do you see this Buddha-land, adorned with such manifold virtues?”
Śāriputra said:
“Indeed, World-Honored One!
That which was never before seen and never before heard is now fully manifested as the adornment and purity of this buddha-field.”
He addressed Śāriputra:
“The buddha-field of my Buddha is eternally pure like this; however, because I wish to bring inferior sentient beings to maturity, I manifest it as a land of immeasurable faults and impurities.”
Śāriputra! It is, for example, like the gods of the Thirty-three Heavens who eat from the same precious vessel, yet the food differs according to what is summoned by their respective karma.
In this same way, Śāriputra!

Innumerable sentient beings are born in a single buddha-field; according to the purity or defilement of their minds, what they perceive differs. If a person’s mind is pure, they will see this land adorned with the wondrous jewels of immeasurable merit.

When the Buddha manifested this adorned and pure land, all five hundred youths brought by Ratnagotra attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), and eighty-four thousand sentient beings all resolved to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
Then the Buddha, the World-Honored One, immediately withdrew his supernormal power, and this world returned to its former state.

Thirty-two thousand devas and humans who sought the vehicle of the śrāvakas, realizing that all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛtadharma*) are entirely impermanent, became free from dust and defilement and attained the purity of the Dharma-eye (*dharmacakṣurviśuddhi*).
Eight thousand bhikṣus were forever freed from all outflows (*āsrava*), their minds being well-liberated.

Chapter Two: Manifesting the Inconceivable Skill in Expedient Means At that time, in the city of Vaiśālī, there was a great bodhisattva of the Licchavi clan named Vimalakīrti. He had already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas and had deeply planted roots of goodness in the presence of those Buddhas. He had attained wondrous eloquence, was endowed with the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), had mastered all dhāraṇīs, sported with supernatural powers (*abhijñā*), and had acquired the power to overcome the forces of Māra and his enemies through fearlessness.

He has entered the profound Dharma-gates and is skilled in the perfection of wisdom; he has mastered skillful means and his great vows are fully accomplished; he clearly understands the inclinations and conducts of sentient beings, and he well knows the superior and inferior faculties of sentient beings.

Having perfected the *Prajñāpāramitā* and matured his skill in preaching the Dharma, he practices with certainty within the Mahāyāna and is capable of skillfully deliberating upon all actions he undertakes.

Abiding in the majestic deportment of a Buddha, he has entered the ocean of mental wisdom; he is praised, extolled, and proclaimed by all Buddhas, and is constantly venerated by Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors. For the sake of bringing sentient beings to maturity, he dwells in the city of Vaiśālī through skillful means.
Possessing inexhaustible wealth, they gather in and benefit the poor, the destitute, and the helpless;
possessing pure precepts, they gather in and benefit all who have committed offenses or transgressions;
through compliant patience, they gather in and benefit those who harbor resentment, violence, jealousy, and malice.
Through great diligence, they gather in and benefit all who are indolent and lazy;
by abiding in meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), right mindfulness, liberation, samādhi, and meditative attainments (*samāpatti*), they gather in and benefit all those with distracted minds;
and through correct discernment (*pratisaṃkhyāna*), they gather in and benefit all those with false views and impaired wisdom.

Though appearing as a layperson, he possesses the dignified deportment and merit of a śramaṇa; though dwelling in a household, he is unattached to the triple world; he manifests having a wife and children while constantly practicing pure conduct, and appears to have a retinue while always delighting in solitude.

Though he wears precious ornaments, his body is adorned with the marks and signs of excellence; though he appears to partake of food, he finds flavor only in meditative concentration and attainment; though he seems to delight equally in gambling and games, he is in truth constantly maturing sentient beings; though he adopts all the rituals of non-Buddhist paths, his aspiration for the Buddha-dharma remains unshakable; though he is proficient in all worldly scripts and treatises, he delights in the Dharma-pleasures within the inner garden of the Dharma; and though he appears among all the assemblies in towns and gatherings, he is always the foremost leader in expounding the supreme Dharma.

In order to conform to worldly conventions, he demonstrates that his conduct toward those of high and low status is never at variance with their expectations; although he does not seek worldly wealth or treasures, he nevertheless shows himself engaged in the pursuit of secular interests.

To benefit sentient beings, he frequents the market streets; to protect the people, he attends to the affairs of kingship; he enters places of debate to guide others with the Mahāyāna; he enters schools to lead and enlighten the ignorant; he enters brothels to demonstrate the faults of desire; and he frequents places of music and entertainment to establish right mindfulness and right awareness.
If among householders, he is honored as the foremost among householders and preaches the supreme Dharma for them;
if among lay devotees, he is honored as the foremost among lay devotees and cuts through their greedy attachments;
if among the kṣatriyas, he is honored as the foremost among the kṣatriyas and teaches them patience.
If among brahmins, he is the most honored among brahmins, eliminating their pride;
if among ministers, he is the most honored among ministers, instructing them in the True Dharma;
if among princes, he is the most honored among princes, demonstrating loyalty and filial piety.
If he is among the inner court officials, he is the most honored among the inner court officials and transforms the palace women toward rectitude;
if he is among the common people, he is the most honored among the common people and cultivates similar merit and superior resolve;
if he is among the Brahmā gods, he is the most honored among the Brahmā gods and demonstrates to the assembly of Brahmās the distinctions of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*).
If he is among the Śakras, he appears as the most honored among the Śakras, demonstrating that all sovereign powers are impermanent;
if he is among the World Protectors (Lokapālas), he appears as the most honored among the World Protectors, safeguarding all benefit and peace.

In this way, the stainless Vimalakīrti benefits sentient beings through such inconceivable and immeasurable gateways of skillful means and wisdom; it was by means of such skillful means that he manifested himself as being ill.
Because of his illness, the king, ministers, elders, householders, brahmins, and others—including the princes and thousands of other officials and attendants—all went to inquire after his health.
At that time, Vimalakīrti, on account of his physical illness, extensively expounded the Dharma, saying:
"O worthy ones!
This body, composed of the four great elements, is impermanent, lacks strength, lacks solidity, and lacks power."
It is decaying and swift, unreliable, a vessel of suffering and affliction, a source of manifold calamities, and subject to the nature of transformation and disintegration.
"O virtuous ones!
Such a body as this is not to be relied upon by those who possess wisdom.
This body is like a mass of foam that cannot be grasped; this body is like a floating bubble that cannot endure for long."
This body is like a mirage, born from the thirst of various afflictions; this body is like a plantain tree, utterly devoid of solidity;
this body is like an illusion, arising from inversion; this body is like a dream, consisting of false perceptions;
this body is like a shadow, appearing through karmic conditions; this body is like an echo, dependent upon various causes and conditions.
This body is like a cloud, changing and perishing in an instant; this body is like lightning, not abiding for even a single thought-moment;
this body has no master, being like the earth; this body has no self, being like water;
this body has no sentient being, being like fire; this body has no life-principle, being like wind; this body has no *pudgala*.
This body is equal to space; this body is unreal, having the four great elements as its abode; this body is empty, being devoid of self and what belongs to a self;
this body is insentient, like grass and wood; this body is inactive, being turned by the power of the winds;
this body is impure, filled with foulness and corruption; this body is deceptive, though it is provisionally covered and sustained by food and drink.
Sustenance inevitably leads to decay; this body is full of afflictions, being a conglomeration of four hundred and four diseases;
this body is easily destroyed, like water cascading down a flight of steps, and is constantly oppressed by decrepitude and old age;
this body is unstable, destined for death; this body is like a harmful enemy, filled everywhere with venomous serpents.
This body is like an empty village, a composite formed by the conjunction of the aggregates, elements, and sense bases. "O noble ones!
You should conceive a sense of weary detachment toward such a body, and you should give rise to joyful aspiration toward the body of the Tathāgata."
Why is this so? The body of the Tathāgata is a collective integration of immeasurable wholesome dharmas;

it is born from the cultivation of immeasurable, preeminent merit and wisdom, and from the cultivation of immeasurable, supreme morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.
It is born from seeing; it is born from the cultivation of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity;

it is born from the cultivation of generosity, the discipline of self-mastery and tranquility, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, liberation, meditative absorption, wisdom, skillful means, aspiration, power, and knowledge; and it is born from the cultivation of all the perfections (pāramitās).
It arises from the cultivation of the six supernormal powers; it arises from the cultivation of the three insights; it arises from the cultivation of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment;
it arises from the cultivation of tranquility and insight; it arises from the cultivation of the ten powers and the four fearlessnesses;
it arises from the cultivation of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; it arises from the abandonment of all unwholesome dharmas and the accumulation of all wholesome dharmas.
"It arises from cultivating the truth and from heedfulness; it arises from cultivating immeasurable, pure karma.
O noble ones! Such are the merits of the Tathāgata’s body; you all should resolve to seek its realization."
If you wish to attain such a body as this and to pacify the illnesses of all sentient beings, you should resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Thus Vimalakīrti preached the Dharma to those who had gathered to inquire after his illness according to their needs, causing countless thousands of people to resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra, Scroll One.
The Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra, Scroll Two.
